# View-Dependent Appearance and Lighting
## Overview
This configuration extends the standard NeRF representation by explicitly modeling the angular dependence of surface appearance and lighting [G]. It sets itself apart from view-independent baselines by separating or jointly encoding directionality into the radiance field, enabling accurate rendering of glossy and transparent scenes [G]. It distinguishes itself from siblings like [UrbanIR](16200-urbanir.md) and [REF2-NeRF](18124-ref2-nerf.md) by focusing on the general architectural conditioning of color on viewing direction, rather than specific inverse rendering or transparency modeling tasks [G].
## Shared principles
The parent article [Model Architecture and Encoding](13550-model-architecture-and-encoding.md) covers the base positional encoding and MLP structure [G]. This family shares the mechanism of conditioning the radiance field's color output on the viewing direction $\mathbf{d}$ [G]. Typically, $\mathbf{d}$ is processed through positional encoding $\Gamma(\mathbf{d})$ and concatenated with position encoding $\Gamma(\mathbf{x})$ before entering the color prediction MLP [G]. The standard volume rendering integral is used, but the color term $\mathbf{c}_i$ at sample $i$ becomes direction-aware [G].
## Subtopics

### [UrbanIR](16200-urbanir.md)
UrbanIR is a method for inverse rendering of large-scale urban scenes from a single monocular video under single illumination. It differs from standard NeRFs by learning intrinsic attributes (albedo, normal) independent of lighting, solving the problem that standard NeRFs bake shading and shadows into observed color, making them non-relightable. Unlike methods requiring multiple lighting sources or LiDAR/multi-camera setups, UrbanIR uses only single illumination RGB video. Choose it for large-scale urban scenes requiring relighting from a single video.

### [See-NeRF](18115-see-nerf.md)
See-NeRF is a unified sensor-physics grounded NeRF framework for sharp High Dynamic Range (HDR) novel view synthesis from single-exposure blurry Low Dynamic Range (LDR) images and corresponding event data. It solves the problem of recovering sharp 3D radiance from degraded inputs by explicitly modeling the physical imaging process of both RGB and event sensors, rather than applying tone mapping directly to 3D points. Unlike sibling methods like REF2-NeRF or EvHDR-NeRF which ignore sensor-physics mismatches, See-NeRF bridges the gap between physical scene dynamics and sensor output using differentiable Camera Response Function (CRF) models for both RGB and event streams. Choose it for HDR synthesis from blurry LDR images and event data.

### [REF2-NeRF](18124-ref2-nerf.md)
REF2-NeRF is a NeRF-based modeling method designed for scenes containing transparent objects, specifically glass cases, where it models refraction and reflection using elements dependent and independent of the viewer's perspective. It estimates surfaces where refraction occurs and separates direct (view-independent) and reflected (view-dependent) light components. Unlike methods that assume straight light rays or only handle reflections, REF2-NeRF handles both refraction and reflection in scenes with multiple transparent objects by using two independent MLPs: a glass network for refraction offsets and a decomposition NeRF for rendering. Choose it for scenes with transparent objects like glass.

### [Unsupervised Decomposition and Enhancement in NeRF](18127-unsupervised-decomposition-and-enhancement-in-nerf.md)
This method decomposes the view-dependent color of a neural radiance field into a view-dependent lighting component $v$ and a view-independent reciprocal color basis $r$, then enhances $v$ using a neural network to produce an enhanced image without ground truth supervision. It sets itself apart from 2D Retinex-based methods by leveraging 3D geometry and multi-view consistency to constrain the ill-posed decomposition, avoiding the need for paired low-light/high-light training data. Choose it for low-light enhancement without ground truth.

### [SAMURAI](18647-samurai.md)
SAMURAI is a joint optimization framework that estimates 3D shape, BRDF material properties, per-image illumination, camera poses, and camera intrinsics from unconstrained in-the-wild image collections with varying backgrounds and illuminations. It addresses the limitations of prior methods like NeRF and Neural-PIL by handling imperfect segmentation masks, arbitrary camera distances, and multiple illumination conditions without requiring correspondences or GAN-style training. Unlike SUDS which focuses on differentiable rendering for inverse problems, SAMURAI specifically targets the decomposition of radiance into shape, material, and illumination from single-view-like unconstrained data. Choose it for unconstrained in-the-wild collections with varying illumination.

### Late Viewing Direction Conditioning
A design choice to fuse the viewing direction only in the last layer of the color MLP [S2]. This prevents the optimization from bypassing the neural voxel to learn a direct mapping from viewing direction to output sample color, which leads to erroneous camera poses and geometry [S2]. Without late viewing direction conditioning, the optimization could minimize photometric loss by optimizing the MLP directly, leading to erroneous camera poses and geometry estimation [S2]. Choose it to prevent erroneous camera poses and geometry during optimization [S2].

### NeRFactor
A method that starts with a pre-trained NeRF model to recover a relightable model by simplifying the pre-trained NeRF’s volumetric geometry into a surface model [S3, unofficial]. It optimizes MLPs to represent light source visibility and surface normals at any point on the surface, and optimizes a representation of the environment lighting and the BRDF at any surface point [S3, unofficial]. Results in a more efficient rendering model because volumetric geometry is simplified into a single surface and light-source visibility at any point can be computed by a single MLP query [S3, unofficial]. Choose it for efficient relightable model recovery from a pre-trained NeRF [S3, unofficial].
